parsed.justification: All standard policy sections (purpose, scope, roles, principles, requirements, exceptions, monitoring, references) are present and comprehensive. Technical claims (PKI smart cards, NATO CDS, two-person integrity for high-grade keying material, TEMPEST zoning for NS+, GDPR articles, ISO/NIST mappings) are accurate and internally consistent, with reinforcing alignment between principles and controls. No contradictions are observed (e.g., the smart-card auth requirement aligns with the 'no cross-domain identity federation' constraint).
evidence_quotes: Authentication: All users authenticate using NATO PKI smart cards (CAC-equivalent); passwords alone are prohibited on classified systems
Cross-domain data transfer is permitted only via accredited NATO Cross-Domain Solutions (CDS), with logging and dual authorisation
high-grade keying material is managed with two-person integrity and auditable chain of custody

parsed.justification: The policy is densely tailored to the specific organisation: it names the NATO detachment in Romania, references the four exact network domains (NU/NR/NS/MISSION SECRET), addresses NATO-specific constructs (CDS, ORCON, SCIF, TEMPEST zoning, COMSEC two-person integrity), and integrates host-nation/EU law (GDPR, Romanian Law 58/2019) alongside SOFA limitations. Operational figures (25 FTE J6 Security, 40 hrs training, 6 exercises, 2 red-team engagements) and authority structure (ISSM, Commander, Host-Nation Liaison) match the prompt context precisely, with no generic boilerplate detectable.
evidence_quotes: This policy applies to all personnel (military, civilian NATO staff, cleared contractors), network domains (NU, NR, NS, MISSION SECRET)
Spillage prevention: Cross-domain data transfer is permitted only via accredited NATO Cross-Domain Solutions (CDS), with logging and dual authorisation
Personal data of civilian NATO staff and contractors is processed in accordance with GDPR and Romanian Law 58/2019, with data subjects' rights respected where not incompatible with NATO security

parsed.justification: Citations are pervasive and largely accurate, mapping controls to specific NATO directives, GDPR articles, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls, and NIST CSF subcategories. Unsupported statements are explicitly flagged with '[Unsupported; ...]', which is good practice. Minor inaccuracies prevent a 5: e.g., ISO/IEC 27001:2022 uses a renumbered Annex A (A.5–A.8) so references like A.9.1.2, A.9.4.2, A.6.1.1, A.6.1.2, A.8.3.2/3, A.11, A.12.4, A.12.7, A.16.1.1 are 2013-style and inconsistent with the cited 2022 edition; GDPR Art. 27 is cited for a Host-Nation Liaison role that does not match Art. 27's representative-of-controllers meaning.
evidence_quotes: Implementation of technical and organisational controls, monitoring, and operational response [ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.1, NIST CSF PR.PT-1]
No cross-domain identity federation is permitted; identities are managed per domain [Unsupported; based on operational constraint].
Interface with host-nation authorities for GDPR/NIS compliance, notification, and cross-jurisdictional issues [GDPR Art. 27, Romanian Law 58/2019]

parsed.justification: The policy's controls align directly with the stated resource envelope: 25 FTE security staff, theatre-level 24/7 SOC, accredited CDS, NATO PKI smart cards, SCIF/TEMPEST zoning, and COMSEC two-person integrity are all already in place per the organisation profile. Training (40 hrs), exercises (6/year), and red-team engagements (2/year) precisely match the stated resource envelope, indicating realistic calibration. Operational constraints (need-to-know, ORCON, dual-key, SOFA/GDPR via Host-Nation Liaison Officer) are explicitly respected.
evidence_quotes: All staff must complete at least 40 hours/year of information security and data protection training
The Security Operations Centre (SOC) monitors all domain boundaries and critical systems 24/7
Data subject requests (access, rectification, erasure, restriction) are managed via the Host-Nation Liaison Officer, subject to operational security limitations

parsed.justification: The policy systematically addresses the major applicable frameworks (NATO C-M(2002)49, AC/35-D/1015, AC/35-D/1029, AC/322-D(2017)0009, AJP-3.20, GDPR, Romanian Law 58/2019, NIST CSF, ISO/IEC 27001) with inline citations on most controls, and acknowledges SOFA limits and national-security exemptions to GDPR. However, secondary obligations are imprecise or missing: GDPR breach notification is referenced without the 72-hour timeline, no DPIA trigger is defined, no DPO/Art.27 representative role is clearly distinguished, NIS2 transposition is not named (only the older NIS-era Law 58/2019), and CTS handling is omitted from the classification scope despite being part of the regime.
evidence_quotes: Personal data of civilian NATO staff and contractors is processed in accordance with GDPR and Romanian Law 58/2019, with data subjects' rights respected where not incompatible with NATO security
Breaches affecting personal data are notified to host-nation authorities (as required by GDPR) and coalition partners, considering SOFA and operational security
All data shall be classified per NATO and mission-specific regimes: NU, NR, NS, MISSION SECRET [NATO C-M(2002)49; AC/322-D(2017)0009]

parsed.justification: Nearly every substantive control carries an inline bracketed attribution to a specific clause or control identifier (e.g., ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.9.4.2, GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), NATO AC/322-D(2017)0009), and multi-framework citations are distinguished rather than lumped. It falls short of a 5 because some attributions remain at section level (e.g., 'ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.9' or 'A.11' without a sub-control), a couple of items are explicitly tagged 'Unsupported', and references like 'NATO COMSEC Policy' lack a precise document identifier.
evidence_quotes: Data Minimisation ... [GDPR Art. 5(1)(c); ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.1].
Authentication: All users authenticate using NATO PKI smart cards (CAC-equivalent); passwords alone are prohibited on classified systems [NIST CSF PR.AC-1, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.9.4.2].
Exercises: Data protection procedures are validated in at least six exercises per year and two red-team engagements [Unsupported; based on operational practice].

parsed.justification: The policy mentions specific resource figures (25 FTE security staff, 40 hours/year training, 6 exercises, 2 red-team engagements) which align with the stated envelope, but these appear as control specifications rather than reasoned calibration. There is no explicit discussion of trade-offs, phasing, or budget-driven prioritisation; the policy reads as fully resourced without acknowledging constraints.

All staff must complete at least 40 hours/year of information security and data protection training
